'''Ranjan Sen''' (born 1967) is an Indian microbiologist, biophysicist and a senior scientist as well as the head of the Laboratory of Transcription at the [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics]]. Known for his studies in the field of [[prokaryotic]] [[Transcription (biology)|transcription]], Sen is an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]. The [[Department of Biotechnology]] of the Government of India awarded him the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to biosciences in 2007.

== Biography ==
[[File:Kolkata univ jeroje.jpg|thumb|125px|left|University of Calcutta]]
Ranjan Sen, born in 1967<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |title=NASI fellows |date=2017-12-21 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2017-12-21 |archive-date=16 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316043224/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |url-status=dead }}</ref> in the Indian state of [[West Bengal]], earned the post-graduate degree of MSc in molecular biology and biophysics in 1991 from the [[University of Calcutta]] and did his doctoral studies on the ''conformational changes of E.coli RNA polymerase during transcription initiation'' under the guidance of Dipak Dasgupta at the [[Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics]] to secure a PhD in 1996.<ref name="CDFD :: Transcription :: Ranjan Sen">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cdfd.org.in/labpages/ranjan_sen.html |title=CDFD :: Transcription :: Ranjan Sen |date=2017-12-27 |website=www.cdfd.org.in |access-date=2017-12-27 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> His post-doctoral work was, first at the laboratory of Nobuo Shimamoto of the [[National Institute of Genetics]] during 1995–98 and later, with Robert Weisberg at the [[National Institutes of Health]] during 1998–2001. On his return to India in 2002, he joined the [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics]] (CDFD) as a scientist. He continues at the institution, holding the position of a scientist grade IV and heads the ''Lab of Transcription'' where he hosts several scientists and scholars.<ref name="CDFD :: Transcription :: Group">{{Cite journal |date=2017-12-27 |title=CDFD :: Transcription :: Group |url=http://www.cdfd.org.in/labpages/transcription_group.html}}</ref> He also serves as the director-in-charge of CDFD.<ref name="Indian fellow - Sen">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P18-1793 |title=Indian fellow - Sen |date=2017-12-21 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-12-21}}</ref>

During his post-doctoral days in Japan, Sen worked on the ''kinetics of abortive transcription in prokaryotes'' and proposed the concept of ''branched pathway during transcription initiation process''.<ref name="CDFD :: Transcription :: Ranjan Sen" /> While in the US, he furthered his work by focusing on transcription [[antitermination]] mechanisms by PUT RNA. At CDFD, the team led by him is involved in the studies of antitermination in [[prokaryotes]], combining physical, chemical, biological and genetic techniques.<ref name="CDFD :: Transcription :: Research">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cdfd.org.in/labpages/transcription.html |title=CDFD :: Transcription :: Research |date=2017-12-27 |website=www.cdfd.org.in |access-date=2017-12-27}}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles<ref name="On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.ca/citations?user=T9bP0v0AAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2017-11-23 |publisher=Google Scholar |access-date=2017-11-23}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of scientific articles has listed 60 of them.<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ranjan_Sen5 |title=On ResearchGate |date=2017-12-21 |access-date=2017-12-21}}</ref> He is also a member of the Task Force on Biotechnology set up by the [[Science and Engineering Research Board]] of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]].<ref name="CDFD :: Transcription :: Research" />

== Awards and honors  ==
The [[Department of Biotechnology]] of the Government of India awarded him the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 2007<ref name="Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development">{{Cite web |url=http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |title=Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development |date=2016 |publisher=Department of Biotechnology |access-date=2017-11-20 |archive-date=4 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304191331/http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> the same year as he was elected as a member of the [[Guha Research Conference]].<ref name="CDFD :: Transcription :: Research" /> The [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] elected him as a fellow in 2011<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=2017-12-17 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2017-12-17 |archive-date=6 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and he received the elected fellowship of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 2017.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017-12-26 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-12-26}}</ref> He is also a recipient of several research fellowships which included GRIP Grant of the [[National Institutes of Health]] (2002), Senior Research Fellowship of [[Wellcome Trust]] (2003) and the Swarnajayanti Fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] (2006).<ref name="Swarna Jayanthi Fellowship">{{Cite web |url=http://dst.gov.in/sites/default/files/sjaward06-07.pdf |title=Swarna Jayanthi Fellowship |date=2017-11-11 |publisher=Department of Science and Technology |access-date=2017-11-11}}</ref>
